title: Revisiting Clustering of Neural Bandits: Selective Reinitialization for Mitigating Loss of Plasticity

problem.claim: Neural clustering-of-bandits algorithms lose plasticity over time, limiting adaptation to non-stationary environments.

gap.claim: Existing CNB approaches do not adequately preserve adaptability in evolving environments.

contributions.claim: SeRe dynamically preserves CNB adaptability by using a contribution utility metric to selectively reset underutilized units while retaining stable knowledge.
An adaptive change detection mechanism adjusts reinitialization frequency according to non-stationarity.
The authors provide a sublinear cumulative regret result for SeRe in piecewise-stationary environments.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Selective Reinitialization as a novel bandit learning framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SeRe enables sublinear cumulative regret in piecewise-stationary environments and outperforms traditional CNB approaches in long-term performance.
The authors report experiments on six real-world recommendation datasets showing lower regrets and improved adaptability and robustness for SeRe-enhanced CNB algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Clustering-of-bandits methods group similar bandits and use cluster-level contextual information for sequential decision-making.
Neural versions of clustering-of-bandits methods suffer loss of plasticity and become less adaptable to changing environments.
SeRe selectively reinitializes underutilized units using contribution utility and adapts reset frequency to detected non-stationarity.
The authors state a sublinear cumulative regret result for piecewise-stationary environments.
Experiments on six real-world recommendation datasets are reported to show lower regrets and improved adaptability and robustness.

source_observation.claim: Selective reinitialization targets underutilized neural units while preserving stable knowledge.

interpretation.claim: Targeted capacity renewal may help non-stationary learners balance adaptation with retention.

application.claim: Consider utility-based selective resets when a neural sequential decision system must adapt without discarding established knowledge.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the utility metric may misidentify units or cause harmful resets.

source_observation.claim: Reset frequency is adjusted according to the degree of non-stationarity.

interpretation.claim: Adaptation schedules can be tied to detected environmental change rather than fixed reset intervals.

application.claim: Use change-sensitive intervention frequency for systems operating under varying rates of distribution shift.

exception.claim: The abstract does not describe the change detector's accuracy, latency, or behavior under incorrectly estimated non-stationarity.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the contribution utility metric.
The abstract does not identify the six recommendation datasets or experimental baselines.
The abstract does not provide regret bounds, numerical results, or details of the piecewise-stationary assumptions.
